objective: Manage asthma and COPD exacerbations with nebulized bronchodilators and CPAP within AEMT scope
secondaryObjectives: Apply CPAP for respiratory distress and recognize when it is failing
Assess oxygenation and ventilation with pulse oximetry and waveform capnography
Generate solutions within AEMT scope and decide when a paramedic intercept is needed

sources.cite: National Registry of EMTs. AEMT examination test plan
sources.note: Relayed from the course seed (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/ems.ts and labs/ems-sources.ts, read in NREMT's own documents 2026-11-09); not re-read for this case. Airway, Respiration and Ventilation: bronchodilators and CPAP within AEMT scope; recognize when CPAP is failing.

sources.cite: NASEMSO. National Model EMS Clinical Guidelines, Version 3.0 (March 2022): Respiratory Distress (Includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema); Airway Management
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in the full text Iowa HHS hosts (https://hhs.iowa.gov/media/198/download) through summarizing fetches with quotes; NASEMSO's own page, read the same day, still presents Version 3 (2022) as current and names no later version. Albuterol nebulized for bronchospasm, repeated for ongoing distress; noninvasive ventilation (CPAP) for severe distress, considered early; start PEEP at 5 cmH2O and raise in 2-3 cmH2O steps to the lowest effective pressure; if the patient worsens on CPAP (worse mental status, rising EtCO2, vomiting), 'remove CPAP/BiPAP and escalate airway management options'; target SpO2 94-98%, and 'permissive hypoxia (SPO2 >= 90%) may be appropriate in patients with COPD'; avoid nitrates within 48 hours of a phosphodiesterase inhibitor. The guideline's albuterol dose for distress (5 mg) is above the inhalation solution's labeled 2.5 mg; the case uses the labeled 2.5 mg dose, repeated.

sources.cite: NHTSA. National EMS Scope of Practice Model 2019: Including Change Notices 1.0 and 2.0 (DOT HS 813 151, 2021-08-01)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17: the record page (title, report number, date; the change notices add intramuscular injection, vaccination in a public health emergency and nasal swab collection at EMT and above) and the PDF's skill tables through a summarizing fetch whose table columns were partly unclear, so placement was checked against the course's own reading (backend/supabase/seed/labs/ems-sources.ts, 2026-11-09) and REQ-241's reading (2026-11-11). EMR: oxygen, BVM, naloxone (intranasal or auto-injector), unit-dose hazmat antidote auto-injectors, tourniquet, wound packing, emergency moves, manual stabilization; no pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring or transport. EMT adds pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring, oral glucose, aspirin, the patient's own nitroglycerin, an inhaled bronchodilator, CPAP, the epinephrine auto-injector. AEMT adds IV and IO access, non-medicated IV fluids, supraglottic airways, waveform capnography, sublingual nitroglycerin and a limited list of IV and IM drugs (dextrose, naloxone). Paramedic adds 12-lead interpretation, manual defibrillation, synchronized cardioversion, transcutaneous pacing, needle chest decompression, intubation and medicated infusions. No newer model was found on 2026-11-17.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

His work of breathing as one severity score: untreated it climbs about 0.012 a minute; each 2.5 mg albuterol nebulizer lowers it 0.08, CPAP 0.02 a minute, BVM assistance 0.03 a minute; 15 L/min oxygen without titration adds 0.008 a minute (carbon dioxide retention in COPD); he becomes drowsy at 0.85 and stops breathing at 1.0. FLAG: authored figures, not a validated model. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

brief.situation: 16:10. You are an AEMT on an ambulance with an EMT partner. Walt, 71, has COPD and called because he can't catch his breath. Worse since yesterday's cold; his inhaler isn't helping.
handover: You carry oxygen, albuterol 2.5 mg nebulizer doses, CPAP, a BVM, a capnograph and a pulse oximeter.
A paramedic intercept can meet you if requested (about 10 minutes); the hospital is 15 minutes away.
Within AEMT scope: oxygen, nebulized albuterol, CPAP, BVM, capnography, IV access. No intubation; paramedics manage advanced airways.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated seconds per real second. Pause any time.
Every assessment and treatment takes the time it would on a real call. Scene time and the drive run on the clock.
Partway through you are asked to explain your decisions in writing. The case ends when care is handed over, then a debrief scores what you did.

safetyNote: Teaching case for exam practice; fictional patient. Not medical advice; follow your local protocols and medical direction.

why.question: What are you treating, how will you know it is working, and what would tell you CPAP is failing?

parts.label: Treatment
parts.criteria: COPD exacerbation with severe distress: albuterol nebulized (labeled 2.5 mg, repeated), CPAP early for severe distress, oxygen titrated to about 90% or more rather than high-flow, capnography.
parts.modelAnswer: A COPD exacerbation in severe distress: albuterol 2.5 mg by nebulizer, repeated, CPAP early at 5 cmH2O and up, oxygen titrated to about 90-92% and capnography to watch his ventilation.

parts.label: Failing
parts.criteria: Worsening mental status, rising EtCO2, slowing or shallow breaths or vomiting mean CPAP is failing: take it off, assist with a BVM, and get paramedics for an advanced airway.
parts.modelAnswer: If he gets drowsy, EtCO2 climbs or he vomits, CPAP is failing: off, BVM assist, and the paramedic intercept for an advanced airway.

expertPath.text: Tripod, three-word sentences, wheeze: severe COPD exacerbation. Oximeter and capnography; albuterol 2.5 mg nebulized; oxygen titrated.
CPAP at 5, raised to 7.5-10; albuterol in line; vital signs.
Load and go; repeat albuterol; notify. If he tires: CPAP off, BVM, intercept.

better.headline: Breathing easier on arrival
better.body: Bronchodilator early, CPAP early, oxygen titrated and capnography watched. That is the expert path within AEMT scope.

arrived.headline: Arrived, by a harder route
arrived.body: Check how soon CPAP went on, whether oxygen was titrated, and how fast you escalated when he tired.

arrest.headline: He tired out
arrest.body: Without early CPAP and bronchodilators, or with CPAP left on a drowsy patient, his breathing stopped. Drowsiness and rising EtCO2 mean escalate: BVM and paramedics.

scoring.modelReasoning: A COPD exacerbation with severe distress: pulse oximetry and capnography; albuterol 2.5 mg nebulized (the labeled dose), repeated; CPAP early, starting at 5 cmH2O and raising in 2-3 cmH2O steps; oxygen titrated to about 90-92% (NASEMSO allows permissive SpO2 of 90% or more in COPD) rather than 15 L/min. Reassess; if he becomes drowsy, EtCO2 rises or he vomits, CPAP is failing: take it off, assist with a BVM and get a paramedic intercept for an advanced airway. Load early, keep treating en route, notify.

target.ask: While the nebulizer runs: what SpO2 are you aiming for in Walt?
target.explain: NASEMSO targets 94-98% in general but says permissive hypoxia (SpO2 90% or more) may be appropriate in COPD; high-flow oxygen can drive carbon dioxide retention.
